title: An interconnection that no longer depends on synchronous machines

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a transmission power system that establishes its own voltage and frequency, remains stable through specified disturbances, detects and clears faults, and restores service without relying on grid-coupled synchronous generators or synchronous condensers. Coordinated power converters would provide the system services that large grids have historically obtained from rotating electrical machines. Grid-forming controls are an existing building block; the target is their integration with protection, energy resources, operating practices and restoration into a convincing system-scale capability.

The exclusion concerns synchronous machines electrically coupled to the grid, rather than every rotating generator anywhere in the energy supply. A full-converter wind turbine can contain a synchronous generator whose electrical behavior is decoupled from the grid by power electronics. Such equipment fits the concept because the grid sees the converter's response. Synchronous condensers do not fit: they supply stability services through grid-coupled rotating machines even though they do not generate energy for sale.

significance.text: Large grids have relied on synchronous machines for important frequency, voltage and fault-response characteristics. Their rotating mass exchanges energy with the electrical system, while their electrical characteristics contribute voltage support and fault current. Converter behavior depends on its controls and equipment limits. Demonstrating that coordinated converters can supply the necessary services at transmission scale would therefore change the engineering basis on which an interconnection can operate. The consequential advance would be a proven replacement for dependence on grid-coupled synchronous machines within a specified operating envelope.

A direct consequence would be the ability to operate that demonstrated system using converter-interfaced generation and storage, including solar, full-converter wind and batteries, provided sufficient energy and equipment capability were available. As a conditional downstream possibility, this could give planners more freedom to retire synchronous equipment or locate new resources without retaining rotating machines solely for stability services. Whether doing so would reduce total costs would depend on the replacement controls, storage, protection, network equipment and operating reserves required.

Scope synthesis: converter-only operation would not establish a fully renewable energy supply, adequate seasonal energy storage or unlimited resilience. Renewable hydro and geothermal generation can use grid-coupled synchronous machines, while converter-interfaced resources still need an adequate source of energy. A large-island demonstration would establish capability at that scale and under its tested conditions; it would not by itself establish continental readiness. Neither universal stability nor operation without operators or central coordination follows from replacing synchronous-machine services.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unresolved integration target is a general, tested way to combine frequency response, system strength, oscillation damping, effective fault detection and clearing, and restoration when grid-coupled synchronous machines provide none of those services. The December 2025 G-PST research agenda documents continuing questions across these capabilities. It supports the existence of substantial engineering work, but does not establish that no complete solution has been demonstrated anywhere by 1 November 2026.

Grid-forming controls already exist, but a programmed converter response is physically different from a rotor's electromechanical response. Converter performance depends on control design, relevant measurements, current limits, available energy and coordination with other equipment. Providing an inertia-like response requires access to energy and sufficient power capability; a control setting alone cannot supply either. Stability must also be assessed across interacting devices and changing network conditions, including damping of oscillations and transitions into current-limited operation.

Protection presents a distinct barrier. Fully controlled wind converters can limit fault current to values comparable with load current, and some conventional overcurrent and directional protection schemes depend on fault-current characteristics such equipment may not supply. The necessary breakthrough is dependable, selective detection and clearing of faults under converter-dominated conditions. It need not reproduce the magnitude or waveform of synchronous-machine fault current if another protection approach can achieve the required outcome.

System restoration adds another integration problem: organizing services that can energize and rebuild a network with few or no synchronous machines and with variable energy resources. Models, stability-assessment methods, equipment specifications and procurement rules must describe capabilities operators can actually rely on. G-PST identifies gaps between what operators know to request, what manufacturers know to provide and the guidance available from standards bodies. Resolving those gaps is part of making the capability repeatable and procurable.

current_state.text: NESO's article dated 11 March 2025 reports the connection of Great Britain's first grid-forming battery and the first two Stability Phase 2 Pathfinder projects going live. It describes ten contracts comprising five synchronous condensers and five grid-forming batteries, securing 11.55 GVA of short-circuit level in Scotland and 6.75 GVA-seconds of inertia for Great Britain. Those quantities describe the contracted portfolio; the article does not establish that all ten projects were operating at publication or attribute the entire portfolio's services to batteries. The synchronous condensers provide stability without generating power, so this is evidence of deployment within a mixed system that retains rotating stability equipment.

The IEEE Power & Energy Society article dated 19 May 2026 reports that IEEE 2800.2-2026, a recommended practice for testing and verifying inverter-based resources, was approved and published in spring 2026. It describes P2800.1 prospectively as a project intended to specify minimum grid-forming equipment capabilities and verification procedures. The project's December 2025 approval is distinct from publication of a completed standard. These statements come from the supplied explanatory article; the review did not establish them through inspection of the standards themselves.

The December 2025 G-PST Research Agenda identifies 48 operator research questions across six programs covering inverter-based resources, stability, distributed resources, control-room operation, services and planning. It describes four years of intensive debate about grid-forming technology and continuing specification and procurement-guidance gaps. Its questions include protection, damping, models, substitutes for inertia and restoration with few or no synchronous machines. The supplied review assessed the complete extracted text, but did not visually inspect figures; the conclusions retained here rely on the text.

The protection reports described in the supplied review include simulations and some field-record validation of wind-plant fault models. These establish useful component-level evidence, rather than operation of an entire converter-based interconnection. Both supplied report extractions were truncated; the C25 report extraction ends on PDF page 64. Its retained passages nevertheless explicitly support the limited-fault-current premise and the distinction between a full-converter turbine's internal generator and its grid-facing electrical behavior.

The earlier research attributed very high instantaneous non-synchronous generation shares in Ireland, Great Britain, Australia, Hawaii, Texas, Tasmania and the Nordic system to a review identified as published on 15 May 2026. It also attributed discussion of fully inverter-based simulation studies to that review. Neither the publisher URL nor the DOI has a retained source artifact in the supplied evidence, so these geographical and study-summary assertions remain unverified here. Their absence from the retained evidence does not establish that they are false. Even a verified high non-synchronous generation share would not alone establish that every grid-coupled synchronous condenser was offline or that the system completed the proposed disturbance and restoration sequence.

Evidence-bound assessment: no inspected text identified in the supplied review establishes the combined transmission-scale fault, separation and black-start demonstration proposed here. The supplied freshness-search record is empty, so worldwide completion status and subsequent developments through 1 November 2026 remain unverified. The record supports deployed building blocks and continuing research needs; it does not establish either worldwide completion or worldwide absence of the complete capability.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: operate a real transmission interconnection, or a large island at transmission voltage, with every grid-coupled synchronous generator and synchronous condenser offline and without external synchronous-system support. Demonstrate severe-fault ride-through, controlled separation and black-start restoration, with selective protection and compliance with the operator's applicable disturbance, island-operation and restoration criteria. This is a proposed integrated benchmark grounded in the documented engineering needs, rather than an established industry completion standard.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed test definition: specify system size, topology, resource mix, available energy, equipment capabilities, operating envelope, fault severity, separation conditions and restoration sequence before testing. Apply frequency and voltage limits appropriate to each energized stage. A blackout and initial energization cannot maintain normal energized-system voltage throughout, so restoration must have its own criteria and milestones. The demonstration should document the absence of synchronous support and record protection actions, converter limits, frequency, voltage and restoration performance.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed test definition

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: repeat the relevant sequences and publish enough operating conditions, measurements, control assumptions and model-validation information for independent assessment. Extend testing across materially different dispatches, network conditions and equipment combinations to establish demonstrated breadth. Practical boundaries should identify the available energy and reserve requirements, permissible outages, fault conditions, current limits and coordination assumptions. Finite tests can demonstrate reliable operation over a defined envelope; they cannot establish literal universality across all inverter mixes or contingencies.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility requirement

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation of results: simulations, hardware-in-the-loop benches, batteries supplying selected services beside synchronous condensers, and mathematical proofs on restricted models would contribute evidence toward the target. None alone completes this field-demonstration proposal. A successful large-island trial would establish a significant bounded capability, while larger networks, other equipment mixes and more demanding contingencies would require additional evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed interpretation of results

related_concepts.text: Roster synthesis — PWR-01, Practical dissipationless conductors and windings for bulk power systems: improved conductors and windings concern losses and equipment performance. PWR-05 concerns how the network establishes voltage and frequency, remains stable, clears faults and restores service. Better conductors could complement such a system, but would not by themselves provide its control and protection capability; PWR-05 does not require dissipationless equipment.

Roster synthesis — PWR-02, Solid-state conversion of heat to utility electricity: this concerns conversion of thermal energy into electricity. PWR-05 concerns the behavior of the interconnected electrical system. A heat-conversion technology could participate if its grid interface supplied the required capabilities, but successful energy conversion would not establish system-wide stability or restoration.

Roster synthesis — PWR-03, Utility-scale electromagnetic delivery of power without a conductor: this concerns the means of delivering power. PWR-05 concerns coordinated operation of a transmission system and does not require conductor-free delivery. Any overlap would arise through the delivery technology's interfaces and their effects on system control, protection and restoration.

Roster synthesis — PWR-04, Site-independent storage from multi-day weather through seasonal imbalance: storage can provide energy for converter frequency response and restoration, but seasonal adequacy is a separate capability. PWR-05 could meet its proposed demonstration using adequate energy over the tested interval without solving seasonal imbalance. Conversely, abundant long-duration stored energy would not itself establish converter stability, selective protection or black-start performance.

Scope synthesis within PWR-05: a single control law proven stable for every inverter mix, or a decentralized architecture resilient to every disturbance without central coordination, would be stronger additional achievements within this entry's technical scope. They do not require separate roster entries here. A coordinated converter grid operating within a demonstrated envelope would already constitute the proposed advance, without proving universal control or eliminating operators.

change_log.change: Defined the excluded equipment as grid-coupled synchronous generators and condensers.
change_log.reason: Full-converter wind turbines may contain synchronous generators electrically decoupled from the grid; excluding every internal synchronous generator would conflict with the intended concept.

change_log.change: Reframed worldwide absence of a general solution as an unresolved completion question while preserving the engineering target.
change_log.reason: The supplied sources document technical challenges, but the empty freshness record cannot establish worldwide incompleteness through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Corrected the NESO article date to 11 March 2025 and distinguished contracted services from operating projects.
change_log.reason: The retained article explicitly supplies that date and reports the first two projects going live, rather than all ten contracted projects.

change_log.change: Preserved the five-condenser, five-battery portfolio and both service quantities with their geographical scope.
change_log.reason: The figures are supported, but describe the mixed contracted portfolio rather than battery-only delivery or a synchronous-machine-free system.

change_log.change: Expressed the protection objective as selective fault detection and clearing rather than mandatory reproduction of synchronous-machine fault current.
change_log.reason: Converter current limits challenge some conventional protection schemes; successful alternative protection can satisfy the functional requirement.

change_log.change: Separated published IEEE 2800.2-2026 from the prospective P2800.1 project.
change_log.reason: Project approval does not establish publication of a completed grid-forming standard, and the supplied evidence is an explanatory article rather than the standards themselves.

change_log.change: Retained the geographical high-share claims and inverter-only study assertions as explicitly unverified attributions.
change_log.reason: The cited review has no retained artifact. This limits verification without proving the assertions false.

change_log.change: Integrated control, energy, protection, coordination, modeling, procurement and restoration barriers into the relevant explanations.
change_log.reason: These scientific and engineering distinctions explain why deployed grid-forming equipment alone does not establish the integrated target.

change_log.change: Revised the completion proposal to exclude external synchronous support and apply stage-specific disturbance and restoration criteria.
change_log.reason: External support could mask dependence on synchronous machines, and normal energized-system voltage limits cannot apply throughout a blackout and black start.

change_log.change: Added explicit repeatability, operating-envelope and scale boundaries to the proposed demonstration.
change_log.reason: A convincing field result needs assessable conditions and reproducibility; finite tests cannot prove universal stability or continental readiness.

change_log.change: Preserved extraction limitations and distinguished component evidence from an integrated field demonstration.
change_log.reason: The protection reports were truncated, G-PST figures were not visually inspected, and simulations or field-validated fault models do not demonstrate the complete interconnection capability.

change_log.change: Explained distinctions with every other supplied roster entry and retained stronger control claims within PWR-05.
change_log.reason: The record must preserve concept identities while separating system operation from conductors, heat conversion, power delivery and seasonal energy adequacy.

unresolved_issues: Whether any transmission interconnection or large transmission-voltage island has completed the combined demonstration worldwide by 1 November 2026 remains unverified; no freshness-search record was supplied.
The claimed geographical high non-synchronous generation shares and the review's account of fully inverter-based studies cannot be checked against a retained artifact.
The supplied evidence does not establish subsequent commissioning of all ten NESO Pathfinder projects or their later operating performance.
P2800.1's eventual publication status and final requirements are not established by the supplied prospective account.
The truncated protection-report extractions limit conclusions about their full coverage; the supplied review did not visually inspect G-PST figures.
Exact demonstration scale, disturbance severity, operating envelope, repeatability requirements and restoration milestones remain proposed parameters to be agreed for a concrete system.
